mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending power and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a contraction in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by high industrial production growth, a sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 105.0 signals strong manufacturing activity that boosts corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 105.0 in a late-cycle expansion regime, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates improving consumer confidence and residential investment, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market that reduces household income and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.0% for three months signals a shift to restrictive policy that dampens economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% in a monetary tightening cycle, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
